title: Radiators and Aftermath
premise: Theo Winterbourne, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost his sense of taste after his father's death, returns to the family's crumbling seaside hotel to settle the estate. Behind a wardrobe he finds a box of letters his mother wrote to a lover she never left—and never sent—revealing that Theo's loyalty to the family myth was built on an arranged silence. As he catalogues the unsaid things of his own life, including his stalled engagement to a woman who deserves honesty, Theo must decide whether to publish the truth in his long-promised memoir or let the family's careful architecture stand. In the end, he mails the letters, loses the engagement but regains his taste at a stranger's kitchen table, and chooses truth over inheritance.
about_author: Rosalind Vasquez is a former hotelier turned novelist who grew up above her family's restaurant on the Yorkshire coast. Her fiction explores the quiet betrayals families commit in the name of love.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A profile piece goes to print describing food he cannot taste; his editor suspects nothing, his fiancée Margot almost does. He keeps a notebook of unsaid sentences. Emotional beat: polished surface over private numbness.

chapters.title: Notice of Estate
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Solicitor's letter summons him to Saltmere House, the family hotel being sold. He hasn't returned since the funeral. Beat: dread disguised as obligation.

chapters.title: Margot Packs Lightly
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. She offers to come; he refuses too quickly. Alone, she finds his notebook of unsent confessions and says nothing. Beat: love shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: Saltmere Off-Season
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The hotel in winter: dust sheets like snow, his sister Imogen already there, brisk and brittle, managing grief through logistics. Beat: siblings circling old wounds.

chapters.title: The Wardrobe
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Clearing his parents' room, a loose panel yields a shoebox—forty years of unmailed letters from his mother, Eleanor, addressed to a man named Callum Reeve. Beat: vertigo of discovery.

chapters.title: Reading by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, interwoven with Eleanor's letter voice. The first letters are joyful, then desperate; she chose the family over him and sealed it away. Beat: intimacy with the dead.

chapters.title: Imogen's Ledger
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. She is hiding debts—the sale must close fast. She notices Theo hoarding papers and assumes worse. Beat: two secrets colliding politely.

chapters.title: Callum Reeve, Still Listed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He tracks Callum to a village forty miles off; the man is alive, elderly, running a chandlery. Theo watches from across the street and leaves. Beat: cowardice rehearsed as caution.

chapters.title: The Taste Test
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At a motorway service station he eats without flavor and realizes the loss began the week after the funeral—after he gave a eulogy full of things he didn't believe. Beat: grief mapped onto the tongue.

chapters.title: Margot Arrives Uninvited
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. She drives north, finds the house half-boxed, senses the letters' existence before seeing them. Beat: tenderness sharpening into demand.

chapters.title: What Mother Asked of Me
chapters.summary: Eleanor's letters dominate; Theo reads her final one, written days before her death, asking whoever finds them to decide 'with kindness, not loyalty.' Beat: the dead hand the living a choice.

chapters.title: Imogen Confronts the Box
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. She discovers Theo reading and erupts: some silences are load-bearing. Their fight cracks open childhood roles. Beat: loyalty weaponized.

chapters.title: Dinner at the Angel Inn
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He interviews himself through a meal he can't taste while Margot watches him fail to perform pleasure. She asks what else he can't feel. Beat: the engagement's fault line exposed.

chapters.title: Callum's Version
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He finally enters the chandlery. Callum knew about the letters, waited decades, and never once wrote back out of respect for her choice. Beat: grace where Theo expected grievance.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Offer
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. A developer's generous offer arrives contingent on discretion—no family history published, no fuss. Signing means burying everything permanently. Beat: money versus memory.

chapters.title: Margot's Ultimatum, Gently Given
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. She doesn't threaten; she simply tells the truth about what loving a man made of omissions costs, and gives him until the sale closes. Beat: heartbreak as clarity.

chapters.title: Drafting the Memoir Chapter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He writes the true story of his parents and his own eulogy lie, tasting nothing all night, then—writing the sentence about his mother's hands—tastes salt. Beat: truth restoring sensation.

chapters.title: The Family Council
chapters.summary: Alternating Theo/Imogen. Uncle Aubrey arrives to broker peace; the siblings argue whether the letters belong to the family, the estate, or history. Beat: climax of duty against truth.

chapters.title: Signing Day
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the solicitor's, pen poised, Theo withdraws the memoir clause demand, lets the sale proceed—but keeps the letters' fate in his own hands. Beat: compromise without surrender.

chapters.title: Mailing the Box
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He posts the letters to Callum, unopened by the world, with a covering note: they were always yours to answer. Beat: release of inherited silence.

chapters.title: What Margot Decides
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. She ends the engagement—not in anger but gratitude—and asks him to write honestly next time. Beat: love that survives only as respect.

chapters.title: A Table for One, Seasoned Well
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Months later, at a stranger's kitchen-table supper club, he tastes lemon, smoke, salt—and weeps into his plate. Final beat: inheritance refused, self inherited instead.
